newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah falls on baht weakness.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah falls on baht weakness.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah fell against the dollar in early trading on Thursday following some weakness in the Thai baht, dealers said.
One U.S. bank dealer said the weakness in the rupiah resulted from renewed pressure on the baht, which spilled over.

The dealer said there was talk that the Bank of Thailand was about to announce its latest foreign exchange reserves figures this afternoon, prompting operators to position themselves if they were below market expectations.
"Speculation in Thailand seems to have driven the rupiah lower and swaps higher," the dealer said.
Spot rupiah fell to 2,590/94 at 0235 GMT from an opening of 2,575/85. Tomorrow and today rupiah were at 2,590.0/94.0 and 2,589.5/93.5, respectively.
Dealers said, however, the dollar appeared to be capped at the 2,600 level on local selling.
"It's regional rather than rupiah trading. You have to look to other currencies in the region before you can have a view on the local market," one local bank dealer said.
Dealers said liquidity remained tight, with overnight rupiah traded around at 17.0 percent.
Overnight swap was at 0.2/0.3 and tom/next at -0.1/par.
One-month swap rose to 16.0/17.0 from 13.0/14.0 on Wednesday, two to 30.0/39.0 from 27.25/30.00, three to 50.0/55.0 from 46.0/49.0 and six to 106/116 from 98.0/100.0.
The central bank kept its intervention band at 2,378/2,682 and the conversion band at 2,559/2,607 on Wednesday.
